thread:
maria: FYI Support ticket from HarborCorp — they reported duplicate 'routing surcharge' lines on last invoice. link: https://support.company/ticket/9432 :grimacing:
aj: can you paste the invoice lines?
maria: redacted snippet:
```\nInvoice lines:
- tokens.model: $73.40\n- cache_credit: -$20.00\n- routing_surcharge: $12.00\n- routing_surcharge: $12.00\nTotal: $77.40\n```
maria: only one active route, no multi-region or fallback configured on their end.
devon: that smells like duplicate emission in the billing pipeline again. we patched a similar issue last year when the router and the prefetch post-processor both emitted the same charge.
aj: running a quick aggregate on invoice_line_items to confirm.
aj: query: `SELECT route_id, charge_code, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM invoice_line_items WHERE customer='harbor' AND window='2026-02' GROUP BY 1,2;`
aj: results show route_main / routing_surcharge = 2 (should be 1).
sam: do we dedupe by deterministic key?
devon: our dedupe uses invoice_id + signature where signature = hash(route, charge_code, model, window, extras). the extras field is populated by postprocessor with attribution tags, so signature diverges.
blake: the postprocessor intentionally generates a separate line for prefetch attribution (helps internal analytics) but that creates an extra billing row for customers that expect consolidation.
maria: ops wants a quick mitigation so we don't have incorrect charge lines sent to customers.
aj: short-term: normalize signature before dedupe by stripping attribution tags from extras. basically `normalized_signature = hash(route, charge_code, model, window)` and dedupe on that. I can ship a tiny exporter patch.
sam: pls be explicit: some enterprise customers lean on the detailed per-source breakdown for their own chargeback. collapsing silently will break them. we need a config flag per-tenant or an "expanded invoice" opt-in.
devon: longer-term plan should be: add explicit metadata `line_source` (router|postprocessor|exporter) on each invoice row and expose `expanded=true` UI mode. then the exporter can control whether to collapse by default.
blake: +1. also add a tooltip in Console: "Routing surcharge appears per-request; expanded view shows breakdown by source."
aj: I'll prepare a PR that implements the normalization under a feature flag `billing.collapse_prefetch_lines`. default ON for public tenants, OFF for enterprise flagged as `needs_expanded_billing`. roll it via canary.
maria: support note: we should proactively notify HarborCorp that we're collapsing duplicate lines and will refund any true double charge. I'll draft.
ops-bot: Incident INC-9432 created (billing-duplicate-lines). Severity: P3.
sam: monitoring plan: emit metric `billing.collapsed_lines.count` and `billing.expanded_lines_requests.count`. alert if collapsed_lines spikes > 1000/hr post rollout.
aj: PR: https://git.internal/exporter/merge/1189 1:18 PST. adding unit test and integration test that simulates postprocessor suffix.
devon: add an integration harness test that runs exporter against sample queue including router + postprocessor emissions and asserts final invoice rows count.
blake: designing the Console toggle now. will post Figma shortly. (link incoming)
maria: schedule: PR -> canary us-east-1 for 30m -> inspect `billing.collapsed_lines.count` and verify no legitimate expanded customers affected -> global.
aj: canary started, will update in ~20m.
sam: support message queued. maria, once HarborCorp acknowledges we can close.
aj: canary report after 18m: collapsed 48 duplicate surcharge lines for HarborCorp window, metric `billing.collapsed_lines.count=48` and no errors. pushing to us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
maria: thanks. follow up Jira for product to decide default UI (compact vs expanded) and add docs to billing FAQ.
devon: reminder: evaluate impact on per-model econ card. if routing surcharge is collapsed, per-model marginal cost metrics need to reflect apportionment. add ticket to ensure the econ pipeline consumes the `line_source` metadata.
maria: noted. closing loop once support confirmation. :white_check_mark:
